newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu aide says five pct shekel slide enough.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu aide says five pct shekel slide enough.

text.p: The government is satisfied with the extent of the Israeli shekel's depreciation but does not want it to continue, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's chief economic adviser said in an interview published on Tuesday.

"We in the prime minister's office are not interested in a 10 percent depreciation of the shekel. There is no need nor is there any reason for a depreciation greater than the five percent that occurred in the week after (exchange rate reform)," Moshe Leon told the daily Yedioth Ahronoth.

"We do not want high inflation. If it continues to rise, the Bank of Israel will intervene and stop it. But I am not giving here advice to the Bank of Israel. They are smart enough to know where, when and how to act," said Leon, who also also serves as director-general of the prime minister's office.
The shekel plunged five percent last week after the government widened the upper limit of the currency's trading band, creating more room for the shekel to depreciate.
This week the shekel has gained back some ground, trading in midsession on Tuesday at 3.568 shekels to the dollar, against a low of 3.592 on Friday.

Regarding privatisation, Leon also said the government planned to complete the sale of its bank shares by mid-1999. The government this year has already sold part of its holdings in Israel Discount Bank and Bank Leumi and hopes to sell a controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim by August.

Leon, who headed a committee on the privatisation of El Al Israel Airlines, said the government would not be able to prevent the carrier from flying on the Jewish Sabbath once it was sold. This prohibition has hurt the airline's profitability.
"It is not possible to privatise El Al any other way," Leon said.

To overcome opposition from religious parties, Leon said he would guarantee that the number of flights taking off and landing at Ben Gurion airport, near Tel Aviv, would not increase after the privatisation.
Leon told the Maariv newspaper that he hoped that airline would be privatised in the first half of 1998.
